verses.author: model_A
verses.text: My grandmother's hands remember a language I never learned.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
flour on the counter
in the shape of no words
I could ever ask her

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the kettle answers
before either of us can—
steam like held breath rising

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
she pours anyway
two cups, no need for a name
for what fills silence

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
her spoon taps twice on the rim—
some old code for *drink, child*
still warm in my mouth

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
outside the window
a bird taps the same two notes—
nobody answers

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the cup cools between us
its steam gone quiet as the bird—
some songs need no reply

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I trace the rim with one finger
where her lips once touched—
the quiet keeps her shape

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the china holds no warmth now
just the memory of holding—
my hands learn her patience

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a crack runs through the glaze—
still the cup stands at the table's edge
learning to hold nothing

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning light finds the crack
traces it like a road home—
the table waits, unbroken

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
dust settles where the sun moved on—
the table's grain remembers every cup
that ever left a ring

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the ring becomes a moon
low over wood grain fields—
someone still sets a place

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
empty chair pulled to the table—
the moon-ring waits for hands
that no longer come home

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
steam rises where no cup sits—
the chair creaks once, settling
into its own patient shape

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the window fogs where breath once was—
someone traces a name in the clouding glass
then lets it fade unfinished
